findings.summary: SupportModalHost hand-rolled a createPortal to document.body at raw z-50 — below the floating-panel band (100) — so a floating panel painted on top of the Support modal and stayed clickable through its full-screen backdrop. CONFIRMED and fixed.
findings.change: Replaced the hand-rolled portal with <Layer tier="modal">, which owns the portal, position and zIndex; className, geometry and the backdrop-click handler carry over unchanged via ...rest. Left a comment recording why check:zindex could not catch this.
findings.verification: An independent verifier that had not seen the auditor's reasoning re-derived the tier table (panel base 100 span 99; modal base 1000), confirmed getLayerHost() returns document.body and setLayerHost() is never called by any app — so <Layer> surfaces and this portal were SIBLINGS in the root stacking context and the raw numbers competed directly — and confirmed Tailwind's z-50 is stock (tailwind.config.js extends only colors). It measured at runtime under Playwright: modal z=50, panel z=100, both parented to body, and document.elementFromPoint over the panel header returned the PANEL, not the backdrop, so the panel both painted above and stayed pointer-interactive. Reachable in all three shipping apps (app-gmt, fluid-toy, gradient-explorer each pass gmtSupportConfig() and mount HelpOverlay alongside DraggableWindow panels). The orchestrator RE-MEASURED after the fix on the same probe: modal z=1000, panel z=100, hit test over the panel header now returns MODAL. typecheck, test:zindex, check:zindex, smoke:help-menu all green. Note the verifier flagged that check:zindex structurally cannot catch this class — its threshold is z >= 100 because it hunts surfaces that outrank the panel band, so a raw z that is too LOW is its blind spot.

findings.summary: smoke:hud-hint was PERMANENTLY RED — its cheatsheet locator used text-cyan-300, a class that no longer exists anywhere in the tree after the runtime-theming rename (ADR-0080) to text-accent-300.
findings.change: Selector repointed to text-accent-300 (HotkeysCheatsheet.tsx:35). Also rewrote the docstring, which described 4 checks that did not match the 5 the file runs (it claimed to look for the Space pill; it looks for the uppercase 'Hotkeys' title), and added the missing assertion on flagAfterH, which was collected and logged but never asserted on.
findings.verification: grep -rn text-cyan-300 returns zero hits tree-wide, so the locator provably matched nothing. The smoke failed at 'hotkeys cheatsheet should be visible by default' (cheatsheet visible at boot: false) before the change and passes all five steps after. It would fail again on a wrong class, because step 1 throws when the locator is empty — which is exactly how this surfaced.

findings.summary: smoke:canvas-menu was PERMANENTLY RED — it asserted the canvas menu contains an item labelled 'Pause', but fluid-toy ships fluidSim.paused: true (pure-fractal boot) so the label always reads 'Resume Sim' at boot.
findings.change: Made the sim-toggle assertion state-independent (/(Pause|Resume) Sim/) with the reason recorded inline. Also implemented the preventDefault check the docstring already claimed: a bubble-phase window contextmenu listener records defaultPrevented (capture phase would run before the canvas handler and always read false), and the smoke now asserts it is true.
findings.verification: Failed before with `menu missing "Pause" (got: ["Copy Julia c", "Resume Sim", "Recenter View", "Reset Fluid Fields"])`; passes after, printing `contextmenu defaultPrevented: true`. The root cause is in files no agent in this run has modified (fluid-toy/features/fluidSim.ts, fluid-toy/pointer/contextMenu.ts), so the failure is pre-existing, not a side effect. The new assertion would fail if contextMenu.ts stopped calling e.preventDefault(), because the window listener reads the flag after the canvas handler has run.

findings.summary: smoke:pause-controls collected the popover text from an unscoped document.querySelector('.text-[8px]') that matched an unrelated menu OnOffBadge, and never asserted on it — so the docstring's claim that it verifies the hover popover exposes the sample-cap slider was entirely unbacked.
findings.change: Replaced the document-wide probe with a locator on the slider's own label text ('Auto-Stop (Samples)') and asserted on it, so a broken or non-opening popover now fails the smoke.
findings.verification: Before the change the smoke printed 'popover footer text: ON', proving the selector matched the wrong element (the real pause popover footer reads '<n> / <cap> samples' or '0 = never stop'), and the value fed no assertion — the smoke could not fail on popover breakage. After, it prints 'sample cap slider visible: true' and hard-fails when false. The label lives inside the showMenu-gated Popover, which is precisely the behaviour the docstring claims to cover. Confirmed across 3 consecutive passing runs. This is the THIRD guard in three cycles found asserting nothing where it claimed to assert something.

findings.summary: check:zindex's body-portal detector missed every createPortal(..., document.body,) written in the multi-line/trailing-comma style, under-reporting by 11 files including engine/plugins/Help.tsx.
findings.change: PORTAL_BODY regex widened to allow the optional trailing comma, with a comment recording why it is load-bearing.
findings.verification: grep for a line-ending 'document.body,' lists 12 files the old regex could not match. check:zindex reported 6 body-portal files before the change and 17 after, still exiting 0 (this report is informational, not failing). The added files are all genuine createPortal call sites, verified by reading the matched lines — no false positives. Notably Help.tsx is one of them, and that file turned out to carry this cycle's Tier V layering bug.

findings.summary: The rule governing engine/plugins/** omitted several files that live there — most importantly Help.tsx, a 559-line slot host no rule mentioned at all — and cited camera/* (one preset-field helper) where the camera plugin is Camera.ts.
findings.change: Rewrote the read-first list to name the slot hosts individually including Help.tsx and RenderDialog/index.tsx; added a paragraph covering engine/plugins/topbar/*, PwaUpdate.tsx and navigation/core/VirtualSpace.ts (navigation.md is scoped to engine-gmt/navigation/**, so that file was rule-orphaned); noted RenderLoop.tsx is deliberately covered by the tick rule; added an Invariants bullet for the global-id registry contract; added smoke:hud-hint + smoke:pause-controls to Guards. Committed together with e08's tiebreak bullet — both auditors edited this file.
findings.verification: grep -rl across .claude/rules/ returns nothing for Help.tsx, PwaUpdate, BucketRender and PauseControls (so they were uncovered) and returns tick-and-animation.md for RenderLoop and navigation.md for navigation — whose frontmatter scopes it to engine-gmt/navigation/**, not this tree. ls engine/plugins/camera/ shows only presetField.ts while Camera.ts sits at the top level with 4 @invariant blocks. The global-id claim is proved by createListRegistry's single keyed Map, by gradient-explorer having to unregister 'fps' before re-slotting it, and by Menu.tsx namespacing anchors as menu:${id}.

findings.summary: TopBar's registration JSDoc tells authors ids need only be 'unique per-slot', but the backing registry is a single global Map<id, item> — the same id in a different slot silently replaces the earlier entry.
findings.change: Corrected the inline comment to 'globally unique; re-register replaces' and expanded the registry comment to state the one-Map-across-all-slots contract, with the unregister-then-re-register workaround and its real call site.
findings.verification: Comment-only, so the proof is grep: createListRegistry does items.set(item.id, item) on a Map created with no slot in the key, and topbar.register passes straight through. Enumerating every topbar.register call site turns up the exact collision the old wording permits — engine registers {id:'fps', slot:'right'} and engine-gmt/topbar.tsx:239 registers {id:'fps', slot:'left'}. No live breakage today, because app-gmt calls installTopBar({hideDefaults:true}) and gradient-explorer unregisters first; the doc was the hazard, not a current bug.

findings.summary: Menu's re-render machinery depends on _bumpRev being the first entry in the _subscribers Set — load-bearing and entirely undocumented.
findings.change: Added an @invariant explaining that _notify iterates in Set insertion order, that this add runs at module evaluation before any component can subscribe, and what breaks if that ordering is disturbed.
findings.verification: Read to the end of the chain rather than inferring: _notify is a forEach over a Set (insertion-ordered); _subscribers.add(_bumpRev) sits at module top level, executing on first import, strictly before any MenuAnchor/MobileMenuHost mount can call subscribe(). Both consumers use a getSnapshot returning _notifyRev, so a stale rev makes useSyncExternalStore bail out of the re-render and menu anchors would stop updating on registration / badge / toggle changes. _bumpRev is never removed — subscribe's teardown deletes only its own fn. smoke:help-menu exercises live menu re-render via the Show Hints toggle.

findings.summary: installSceneIO's capture invariant enumerated five of the six captured options, omitting _onBeforeSerialize, and did not mention that install-time-baked menu labels do not follow a reinstall the way render-time reads do.
findings.change: Added _onBeforeSerialize to the list and appended the asymmetry: the Save Scene label freezes at first install while LoadSceneMenuItem, which reads the module value at render time, follows a reinstall.
findings.verification: Grep-provable: all six module vars are assigned before the `if (_installed) return;` short-circuit, so _onBeforeSerialize belongs in the list. The asymmetry is read off two adjacent sites — the label interpolates _fileExtension once during registration, while LoadSceneMenuItem interpolates it inside its render body.

findings.summary: Hud's JSDoc says 'Slots are always rendered', which the host contradicts twice: an empty slot returns null, and the region prop documented eight lines below drops whole slot rows.
findings.change: Restated the intent accurately — every slot is available without setup, a slot with no visible widgets renders nothing, and region can drop whole rows from a given host.
findings.verification: Read to the end of HudHost: an `items.length === 0` early return inside the slot map, and slotsToRender narrowing to 4 or 3 of the 7 slots when region is 'top' or 'bottom'. smoke:hud-hint asserts on HUD widget presence and disappearance through the when predicate.

TWO GUARDS IN THIS SUBSYSTEM WERE RED BEFORE THE AUDIT TOUCHED ANYTHING, both from stale expectations rather than broken product code: smoke:hud-hint (class renamed by the ADR-0080 theming pass) and smoke:canvas-menu (fluid-toy's pure-fractal boot default inverted a menu label). CONCURRENT-RUN INTERFERENCE: other auditors were editing app-gmt/main.tsx, engine/AdaptiveResolution.ts, engine/plugins/Shortcuts.ts, engine/plugins/Viewport.tsx, ViewportFrame.tsx, viewportSlice.ts and types/viewport.ts while this auditor ran browser smokes. Every failure of that shape re-ran clean and none was counted as a finding; each smoke was re-run to a stable pass at the end. The orchestrator additionally re-ran smoke:undo twice on the quiescent tree after all auditors returned — both passed, confirming the e08 flake was the same HMR artefact.

ONE SUSPICION CHASED AND DROPPED: the pause button's third title state ('Done — N samples') would evade the smoke's locator, but a runtime probe shows accumulationCount reaches only ~2 after the smoke's 3s boot wait against a sampleCap of 64, so it is unreachable there and not worth a change.

SCOPE COVERED: all @invariant blocks in Hud/TopBar/Menu/Help/SceneIO/PwaUpdate/RenderDialog/topbar (the Menu, SceneIO and RenderDialog ones all hold as written apart from the SceneIO omission); citation drift across those files (they carry no @see citations at all, so nothing to break); five smokes plus zindex/orphans/typecheck.
